title: Specify how representation translates into decision influence
requirements:
- Describe mechanisms that give represented groups genuine influence (decision rights, transparent selection, agenda-setting, feedback obligations)
- Extend the examples to persons with disabilities, older people, linguistic minorities, Indigenous communities, children, people without legal identity, the digitally excluded and caregivers
- Require involvement of health workers, communities and subnational authorities across the lifecycle
- Address subnational, frontline and community participation, not only national bodies
- Ask countries to identify under-represented groups through a contextual assessment rather than a fixed list
- Offer a non-prescriptive multi-party governance pattern countries may adapt
